question: What PHB yields on glucose have been reported, and how far are they from the ceiling?

claims.text: Flux balance ceiling for PHB made from glucose in the E. coli K-12 central-carbon core model, with the phaCAB add-on route; this is a computed upper bound with no time axis or vessel.

Flux balance ceiling for PHB made from glucose in the genome-scale E. coli K-12 MG1655 model (iJO1366), with the phaCAB add-on route; this is a computed upper bound and is higher than the core-model ceiling.
A recombinant Escherichia coli strain was reported to produce PHB from glucose as sole carbon source at a volumetric titre, not a yield per glucose.
The corpus contains no reported PHB yield on glucose in grams per gram for an engineered Escherichia coli strain, so a direct comparison with the E. coli ceilings cannot be made.

gaps: No record in the corpus gives a PHB yield on glucose in grams per gram for an engineered E. coli strain; the only E. coli glucose PHB figure is a titre (cl1-P17-6efa5b8a), so the gap to the ceiling cannot be measured for E. coli.

The yeast yields in P24 are reported in milligrams PHB per gram glucose, while the ceilings are in grams per gram; a unit-consistent record of the yeast yield is needed to state how far below the ceiling it lies.

The ceilings are flux balance upper bounds with no time axis, vessel or process; no measured fed-batch or batch PHB yield on glucose from the same host and process is in the corpus to set against them.
Glucose-only yields for PHB in Pseudomonas, Bacillus or Ralstonia hosts were not found as records; the R. eutropha yield found (P6) is on a glucose plus xylose hydrolysate, not glucose alone.
rejectionReasons: c3: a quote that is not a whole sentence or row of P24:t1:2
a gap dropped: it holds a number
